title: Week-numbered range controls treat a week the year does not have as a real value
text_original:
- Ensure custom selectors or namespace dictionaries reject non-string keys
- Fix handling of `:in-range` and `:out-of-range` with end of year weeks
- Fix a potential infinite loop in pretty printing of compiled selector objects
text_rewritten:
The :in-range and :out-of-range states on a week-numbered range control accept a value naming week 53 of a year that only runs to 52 weeks, and then compare that non-existent week against the control's limits. The control ends up reported as out of range, which reads as a data error in our validation report when the real problem is that the value is not a week at all.

A value that names a week the year does not have is not a comparable value, so the control should be treated exactly like one that carries no value -- which this library already reports as in range. Years that genuinely do run to a fifty-third week must keep comparing normally, controls with ordinary in-range and out-of-range values (week or date) must not change, and the two states must stay mutually exclusive.
body:
The :in-range and :out-of-range states on a week-numbered range control accept a value naming week 53 of a year that only runs to 52 weeks, and then compare that non-existent week against the control's limits. The control ends up reported as out of range, which reads as a data error in our validation report when the real problem is that the value is not a week at all.

A value that names a week the year does not have is not a comparable value, so the control should be treated exactly like one that carries no value -- which this library already reports as in range. Years that genuinely do run to a fifty-third week must keep comparing normally, controls with ordinary in-range and out-of-range values (week or date) must not change, and the two states must stay mutually exclusive.
acceptance_hint: A week value naming a week number the year does not have counts as no value at all for the two range states; years that really have a fifty-third week still compare normally, and no control is ever reported in both states.
